# Welcome {#sec-presentacion .unnumbered}

This book accompanies the course **Digital Skills for Information Use** (*Competencias digitales para el uso de la información*, code 19408, 3 ECTS, first year, second term), part of the Bachelor's degree **Transversal Training** programme (*Formación Transversal*) at Universidad Carlos III de Madrid. Its aim is to help you **find, evaluate and use information reliably and ethically**, including when it is produced by artificial intelligence.

The book follows the four blocks of the official syllabus: evaluating the credibility of digital information, searching for and organising information, using it ethically (including references and plagiarism) and generative artificial intelligence for content creation.

This is the English edition of the book. The [Spanish edition](https://pablosancheznunez.com/competencias-informacion/) has the same content.

**Author:** Pablo Sánchez-Núñez, Universidad Carlos III de Madrid\
**ORCID:** [0000-0001-7845-9506](https://orcid.org/0000-0001-7845-9506)\
**Website:** [pablosancheznunez.com](https://pablosancheznunez.com)

**DOI:** [10.5281/zenodo.24550050](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24550050).

## Course objectives

By the end of the course you should be able to:

- Recognise information overload and disinformation, and use digital information critically.
- Identify, select and evaluate information sources, including social media as a source of scientific information.
- Design search strategies on general and specialised platforms, and organise what you find.
- Use information ethically, respecting intellectual property and avoiding plagiarism.
- Create and manage references with a citation style.
- Understand how generative artificial intelligence works, what it is useful for, what its limits are and what ethics and regulation say about its use.

## How each chapter is organised

Each chapter begins with **objectives** and a **glossary**, suggests a **required reading** and further readings, develops the **contents** of the syllabus, proposes a **practical exercise** and an **assessed challenge**, and ends with a **self-assessment** with instant feedback and **further resources**.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false"}
## A little R
Four chapters include very short R exercises that run in your browser without installing anything, so you can look inside some tools: the Boolean operators of a search engine, the format of a reference, detecting overlaps between texts or checking references generated by an AI. You do not need to know how to program: the chapter [Using R in this book](00-r-in-this-book.qmd) explains the essentials, and every exercise has a hint and a solution.
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" icon="false"}

## Your progress and offline use

The book records the exercises you solve and the questions you answer correctly. Your progress is stored **only in this browser**: it is not sent to any server and teaching staff cannot see it.

::: {#progreso-resumen}
Turn on JavaScript to see your progress.
:::

After your first visit, the browser keeps a copy of the book and the R engine, so you can read the chapters you have opened **offline**. [If your browser supports it, this is enabled when the page loads.]{#sin-conexion-estado .sin-conexion-estado}

Use the switch next to the book title, in the sidebar, to change between light and dark mode.

## Assessment

The course is taught in person with **continuous assessment (100 %)**: practical assignments and presentations (**70 %**) and a **final test** on the last day of class (**30 %**), in which you need at least 4 out of 10. Attendance and participation may count. Plagiarism or copying in any activity means losing the mark for that activity.

- Each chapter's **assessed challenges** are designed as practical assignments.
- The **self-assessments** do not count towards your mark and prepare you for the final test; they are also available in Aula Global.

This summary follows the official course description; if there is any difference, what the course publishes in Aula Global prevails.

## Core bibliography

- Bobish, G.; Jacobson, T. (eds.) (2014). [*The information literacy user's guide: An open, online textbook*](https://milnepublishing.geneseo.edu/the-information-literacy-users-guide-an-open-online-textbook/). Open SUNY Textbooks.
- Cordón García, J. A. et al. (2016). *Las nuevas fuentes de información: la búsqueda informativa, documental y de investigación en el ámbito digital*. Pirámide.
- Cruz Gil, C. (2015). *Modelos de búsqueda y recuperación de la información*. Trea.
- Dorner, D. G.; Gorman, G. E.; Calvert, P. J. (2015). *Information needs analysis: Principles and practice in information organizations*. Facet.
- Pacios Lozano, A. R. (coord.) (2013). *Técnicas de búsqueda y uso de la información*. Ramón Areces.
